title: Grants by design
sub: The fourth film of Only what you may see, the second series of Data protection and privacy: why the Galápagos could take in more visitors every year and keep their animals safe, by planning the visits once for the whole park, with most of it closed, a few sites along marked trails, a guide with every group and the same rules for everyone; and the same for data in Unity Catalog: three rights to read a table, shelves by who reads them, grants only to groups and only on a catalog or a shelf, so every new table is read by the right people from its first minute, owners that are groups, catalogs bound to the workspaces they may be read from, and the whole plan kept as code, approved by the data's owner.
howto: The film is drawn in the module's look, Night glass: a dark hall of frosted panes, frosted where what's behind may not be read and clear where it may. The registrar's catalog is a room of glass with its shelves, each a pane that clears for the groups that may read it. Cyan is an identity, green allowed, coral denied or closed, amber power switched on, violet hidden personal data, grey what needs no protection. GitHub's and Databricks' pages are drawn as their docs show them, with their logos. The Galápagos of the 1970s are painted in the same evening light, with their place and year on a tag.
